title: [Design and implementation of a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To designe a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology and to conduct preliminary applications, achieving the protection of patient privacy and promoting the safe use of clinical image data in clinical trial projects. METHODS: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology was first performed to preprocess operations, such as cropping and compression on medical images to initialize the image records. Then, it utilized advanced image recognition, natural language processing, and convolutional neural network technologies to automatically classify (labeled, feature extraction, and text recognition) according to the content of medical documents. It automatically identified sensitive information in the image records of clinical trial patients, including personal identity information such as patient name, identification number, medical record number, phone number, and birthplace. Pixel-level masking or blurring was performed on the identified sensitive information points, and an artificial online desensitization system based on canvas technology was assisted to ensure the security and confidentiality of privacy data. RESULTS: The designed clinical trial image record desensitization system exhibited high performance and efficiency in both desensitization effect and processing speed. After desensitizing 100 000 pieces of image record data in this system, a total of 9 000 medical record image samples were randomly selected from the processed medical document types for automated desensitization effect verification. The average accuracy rate of medical document desensitization reached 88.48%, with an accuracy rate of up to 99.40% for serious adverse event medical documents. CONCLUSION: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology improves accuracy and efficiency in medical data privacy protection. Combined with the artificial online desensitization auxiliary system, it can be applied in production environments, providing reliable technical support for the safe sharing and effective utilization of clinical trial image records.

title: dermsr: a reference implementation of the DERMS-R model-selection score
abstract: Initial release of dermsr, the reference implementation of the DERMS-R model-selection score, implementing the "Reproducibility and Reference Implementation" section of the companion paper (Ramos, 2026). derms_score(...) with the paper's exact documented signature DERMSRScorer, a reusable scorer for raw cross-validation fold accuracies Sensitivity-analysis scenarios (Table 5) and statistical comparison tools (Friedman test, Iman-Davenport correction, Nemenyi critical difference) Functions reproducing the manuscript's Tables 2-6 from raw results A bundled, verified 12-architecture x 5-ratio CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset, so reproduction scripts and tests are fully self-contained 47 tests (43 unit + 4 doctests), using published paper values as fixtures rather than invented examples MIT licensed See README.md for usage and scripts/ for runnable reproductions of the manuscript's tables and statistical analyses.

title: Research Package: Mitigation of Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed in High-Dimensional Transformer and Latent Diffusion Architectures
abstract: Contains the theoretical paper formalizing Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed (CSSB) along with an automated PyTorch/Hugging Face validation framework script. CSSB occurs when high-dimensional transformer matrices inadvertently map semantically unrelated domains into overlapping vector trajectories, leading to hidden downstream reasoning degradation or alignment drift. The provided pipeline implements Layer-wise Linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) scanning [cite: 1], multi-step Shannon entropy tracking [cite: 1], and causal null-space ablation interventions (\(P = I - vv^T\)) to mitigate cross-attention attribute binding and linear refusal circuit interference.

title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

title: Break-even analysis of risk-based trade screening: per-route test scores and analysis code (reproducibility materials)
abstract: Reproducibility materials for the article "When Screening Does Not Pay: Break-Even Conditions for Risk-Based Trade Inspection under Extreme Class Imbalance" by Sushanta Paul (National Board of Revenue, Bangladesh). Contents: (1) per-route test scores of five detectors (interpretable triadic residual, its logistic readout, local outlier factor, isolation forest, gradient boosting) with injected-anomaly labels for 7,637,362 candidate routes, one training seed, deposited in 15 parts with SHA-256 checksums; (2) analysis scripts that compute the exact operating characteristic, break-even hurdle, optimal inspection budgets, a negative-subsampling prevalence test, a test-set bootstrap, and the figures; (3) the exact result tables. See README.md for reassembly and run order. The scores were generated with the code of the triadic trade-anomaly screening benchmark (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20513788), built from public UN Comtrade and CEPII GeoDist data.

title: Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers — Reproducibility Package
abstract: Source code and saved-result reproducibility material for Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers, by Jianfeng Chen (Independent Researcher). Qstreams maintains multiple residual streams with explicit Q/K/V read-role biases. This release includes 36 implementation/runtime packages, fixed protocols, 54 conditions and 162 trained-model identities, all 279 paired comparisons, per-window independent T1 test measurements, 243 read/write intervention conditions, 5,628 signed-FFN diagnostic conditions, and the separate F1 support study. CPU tools verify saved statistics, construct the architectures, and regenerate manuscript figures. Archive download: Zenodo stores the complete accepted ZIP as seven binary transport parts (.part001 through .part007). Download all seven parts, ZENODO-PARTS.json, and assemble_qstreams.py into one directory, then run python assemble_qstreams.py. The script verifies every part and reconstructs the original qstreams-reproducibility-v1.zip. See README-ZENODO.txt. A single-file download is also available from the GitHub release. The reconstructed ZIP is the byte-identical accepted 15 October 2026 export: 138,653,259 bytes, 891 members, SHA-256 38cbf14a0e0993e4e4aed798897ea6ee615407fa470a8a28fe59fef72f838654. It includes the historical document-exclusion hash indexes. The accompanying publication revision adds hosting links. Trained weights, corpus text, and token shards are not included; checkpoint inventories, hashes, loaders, and upstream input identities are provided. Fresh GPU runs require those external inputs and separate environment qualification. GitHub: https://github.com/eatkeyboard/qstreams. License scope: original software is Apache-2.0; the manuscript, original figures, documentation, and derived result tables are CC BY 4.0. These are component-specific licenses, not a choice of licenses for every file. Third-party dependencies and source datasets retain their own terms; see NOTICE, LICENSE-CONTENT.md, and THIRD_PARTY.md. All training seeds, counterexamples, and original numerical labels are retained (91 passed / 71 finite numerical failures in AT1). Full-sequence scoring admissions are documented separately. Test document exclusion is exact-document matching; it is not a guarantee against semantic or near-duplicate overlap. Mechanism measurements use specified development windows. Recomputations operate on saved measurements and do not reconstruct unsaved activations or gradients.

title: ChunavIQ: an open, end-to-end verifiable remote-voting research prototype for India
abstract: Research prototype of an end-to-end verifiable, secret-ballot online election adapted to Indian law, identity infrastructure and scale: deniable revoting with a polling-day override, Aadhaar-or-PAN registration, one national threshold key held in hardware security modules, Terelius-Wikström verifiable shuffles, two independent verifiers (Python and TypeScript), a national-scale capacity model from measured unit costs, and open adversarial dress rehearsals with every request published. Includes the paper (paper/ChunavIQ-paper.pdf). Synthetic data only; not certified or authorised for any binding election. Live demo: https://chunaviq.oglic.com

title: Pre-registration: PVBRF-ID versus FedAvg and multi-Krum under a 30% adaptive attacker (arXiv 2610.12704, 10 fresh seeds)
abstract: Frozen pre-registration (18 Oct 2026) of an independent replication of the adaptive-attacker result in arXiv 2610.12704 (PVBRF-ID): on Edge-IIoTset with 10 simulated sites and 3 of 10 sites mounting the authors tolerance-exploiting adaptive attack, over 10 fresh seeds (10-19), whether PVBRF-ID (tau -0.3, secure clipping) exceeds FedAvg in final macro-F1 by at least 0.40 and is not more than 0.10 below plaintext multi-Krum (paired 95% t-interval lower limits; the paper reports +0.595 and -0.052). Files: PREREG.md (protocol, rule, controls, disclosure), decide.py (rule and planted-effect table), harness.py (analysis), kernel_pv.py (CPU kernel running the authors supplementary notebook with overridden seeds/arms). Deposited BEFORE the main kernel is run. Verdicts: Replicated / Did not replicate / Inconclusive under protocol X.

title: The Memory of Carbon and the Silence of Absolute Zero: An Interdisciplinary Proof of the Next-Generation Decentralized Autonomous Security "Yuki-Onna Protocol" Based on the Physics of Subtraction
abstract: Contemporary frontier quantum computing architectures spearheaded by Silicon Valley hyperscalers (such as Google's Willow superconducting processor) rely fundamentally on an engineering paradigm of "the Logic of Addition" (足し算の論理): stacking multi-stage dilution refrigerators, expending thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit in surface-code Quantum Error Correction (QEC), and continuously injecting active microwave control pulses to suppress noise. However, as coaxial control lines scale, Johnson-Nyquist thermal noise ( = 4 k_B T R Delta f) and the fundamental thermodynamic cost of quantum measurement and syndrome erasure under Landauer's principle (Delta Q_meas >= k_B T ln 2 per bit) generate an insurmountable thermal spiral against unauthorized external probing. In contrast, this monograph establishes the foundational theory of next-generation Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS: 自律型分散セキュリティ) grounded in "the Physics of Subtraction" (引き算の物理学)—designated the "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (雪女プロトコル). Rather than expending external power to actively suppress noise, the Yuki-Onna Protocol passively drains and absorbs the excess computational heat injected by an intruding observer (hacker), forcing the adversarial probe into irreversible decoherence and absolute-zero silence. The physical core of this cyber-physical defense matrix is not a synthetic metamaterial, but 3 x 10^8-year-old "Memory of the Earth" (大地の記憶): Carboniferous coal measures in the Pennine Range of Northern England compressed by the Variscan Orogeny (~390–300 Ma) and thermally metamorphosed by the 1200°C quartz-dolerite magma intrusion of the Great Whin Sill into devolatilized semi-anthracite and Natural Coke (天然コークス). Exhibiting elevated vitrinite reflectance (R_o) and maximal Bond-Network Entropy (S_BN) across its nanoporous defective-graphite topology, this carbon matrix supports hydrodynamic Second Sound thermal wave propagation (v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R)) coupled with multiscale boundary scattering. Integrating open quantum system Lindblad dynamics with a non-Markovian Sub-Ohmic phonon bath (J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1), we prove that any unauthorized quantum measurement triggers continuous environmental heat extraction, locking the attacker's wavefunction via the Quantum Zeno Effect and condensing extracted thermal energy into a driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) limit cycle of infinite futility. 【和文標題・要旨】 『炭素の記憶と絶対零度の静寂:引き算の物理学に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ「雪女プロトコル」の学際的証明』 現在、シリコンバレーの巨大テクノロジー企業群が牽引する量子コンピューティングの最前線(GoogleのWillow等)は、複雑な希釈冷凍機を重ね、表面符号等の誤り訂正に膨大な物理量子ビットを投じ、マイクロ波パルスを絶え間なく注入してノイズを押さえ込む「足し算の論理」に深く依存している。しかし配線群からのジョンソン・ノイズや、ランダウアーの原理に基づく量子測定・情報抽出(ハッキングを含む)そのものが伴う不可避な熱放散(k_B T ln 2)により、既存の能動的冷却機構では侵入者が引き起こす局所的・突発的な熱的スパイラルに追従できない。これに対し本論文は、外部エネルギー注入でノイズを押さえ込むのではなく、侵入者(観測者)が持ち込む過剰な演算エネルギー(熱)をシステム自体が受動的に「吸い尽くし」、系全体を情報の不可逆的散逸と絶対零度の静寂へと強制還元する「引き算の物理学」に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ(DAS)――「雪女プロトコル(Yuki-Onna Protocol)」――を学際的に証明する。その物理的コアは、約3億年前のバリスカン造山運動とグレート・ウイン・シルの約1200℃のマグマ接触変成作用によってイギリス・ペニン山脈に形成された「天然コークス(ナノ多孔質・欠陥グラファイト炭素結晶)」である。数億年の「大地の記憶」が刻んだボンドネットワーク・エントロピー(S_BN)とフォノン流体力学的な第二音波(v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R))の結合により、侵入熱は波として炭素深部へ引きずり込まれて減衰・吸収される。さらにサブオーム的スペクトル密度(J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1)を持つ非マルコフ的リンドブラッド散逸方程式と量子ゼノン効果・ボース=アインシュタイン凝縮(BEC)を統合し、攻撃者の演算リソースを「絶対零度のノイズ」と無限の徒労(リミットサイクル)へと陥れる完全受動的物理防衛マニフェストをここに構築する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

title: Generative Structural Theory v1.19 — The K1c Roots of the GST v1.18 Certificates: What the Records Show, and a Conditional Procedural Account of the Stored Answer
abstract: This study examines the recorded root answers in two GST v1.18 certificate files. At three distinct residuals, comprising four arc–residual pairs classified as K1c, the recorded answer is y = z_t − {1>3}, rather than z_t. It separates two questions: whether (X′, z_t) belongs to the recorded acceptance relation, and which procedure fixed the stored answer.A registered reading finds both (X′, y) and (X′, z_t) in the recorded relation at all four target pairs. The relation’s closedness rests on the earlier verification record, subject to the stated provenance limitations. A comparison of the fixed certificate and targets files also confirms agreement of the target value adopted by the evaluator’s and extractor’s rules.Static examination of specified code versions shows that the generator stores the candidate of least cut value, the verifier checks the stored answer without selecting it, and the extractor transcribes it. This yields a conditional procedural account: if the generator version examined wrote the stored answers, y was its least candidate. It does not establish mathematical uniqueness.The contemporaneous records examined do not fully establish which code versions the past runs executed. The actual generator candidate sets remain unknown, and applications of the cited lemmas retain the stated cone-membership condition. The structural questions associated with the v1.18 open item O1 remain unresolved.The supplementary archive contains the cited working records, including corrections and addenda, with a records table and SHA-256 manifest. Their inclusion does not constitute independent verification of their contents.

title: Choosing Evidence Before Answering: Single-Retrieval Decisions RAG versus Embedding-Only RAG
abstract: Embedding similarity identifies passages related to a question, but topical similarity does not establish answer support. We evaluate a fixed single-retrieval policy that scores embedding candidates against an explicit four-level support rubric using the OpenAI Decisions API, then selects evidence under a fixed threshold and token budget. The method is unchanged throughout the study. The main evaluation compares this policy with the application's embedding-only selection in paired runs on 600 newly sampled MuSiQue-Ans development questions. Both arms use the same native research worker and qualitative writer; only the Decisions feature gate differs. The sample excludes previously evaluated question IDs and exact normalized questions and targets a fixed 58/25/17 mixture of two-, three- and four-hop questions. The Decisions policy obtains mean automated, quote-extracted answer-content F1 46.66 versus 39.75 for embedding-only selection. The paired mean difference is +6.91 points, with nominal 95% hop-stratified bootstrap interval [+3.65, +10.27]. F1 measures normalized answer-token overlap. Higher F1 with 47.83% fewer selected passages (2.61 versus 5.00 per question) shows a favorable observed trade-off between answer overlap and selected evidence quantity. Annotated support recall is lower (60.82% versus 70.99%); factuality and citation entailment were not assessed. Post-hoc accounting of successfully metered API usage, including corpus and query embeddings, scoring, research and writing, estimates 38.03% higher cost for the same 600-question workload under the observed cache behaviour. A complementary, previously frozen 200-question HotpotQA study with a standardized short-answer reader finds an F1 gain of 8.30 points (nominal 95% paired interval [2.97, 13.72]). Equal-count and common-budget diagnostics support a useful ranking signal in that setting. These results concern evidence selection from supplied local paragraph pools, not full-corpus retrieval. Shared sources, public benchmark exposure, automated answer extraction, one model family and the absence of new human adjudication limit the claim. Conditional on the saved generations and stated resampling assumptions, the fresh comparison supports a positive answer-content F1 difference; unresolved source dependence limits population inference, and a gain exceeding the five-point working practical margin is not established. Working paper / preprint; not peer reviewed. The companion Source_and_Evidence.zip contains the frozen sample, protocols, saved outcomes and numerical reanalysis tools. It documents its reproduction boundaries and does not distribute the full private application or enable independent regeneration of native answers. Funding: no external research funding reported. Competing interests: none declared by the author.

title: FEDERATED SWARM LEARNING FOR PERSONALIZED BCI AT THE LIMIT STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 23 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION (COPY-READY) Can brain–computer interface systems learn from multiple laboratories and microrobotic sensing platforms without transferring raw neural recordings, reproducing device-specific shortcuts, or sacrificing the least-represented participants? This research monograph explores that question through the coupling of local swarm learning, privacy-preserving collaboration, and out-of-site generalization. The volume treats federation as a testable scientific and governance architecture—not an automatic privacy guarantee. It distinguishes confidential transport, secure aggregation, formal differential privacy, machine-unlearning claims, and genuine downstream withdrawal of model influence. It examines non-identically distributed neural data, sensor drift, personalized calibration, negative transfer, client-level poisoning, subgroup equity, and the difficult question of who may authorize a model update or a subsequent BCI-mediated action. Its research structure includes 30 linked mathematical derivation and definition plates; 82 chapters, each with five separately paginated research sections; 200 detailed Research Gates that offer future investigators falsifiable experimental entry points; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos designed for revision, disconfirmation, and scientific handoff. A 20-record DOI evidence ledger anchors established methods while keeping proposed neurovascular microrobot integrations clearly distinct from demonstrated evidence. The central research challenge is not simply to improve average federated accuracy. It is to determine when shared structure remains predictive at previously unseen sites, when local autonomy is the scientifically stronger answer, and when the responsible choice is to abstain, revert, or retire a model. This is a non-clinical, hypothesis-generating research atlas, not evidence of validated human neurovascular microrobots, a clinically proven BCI, or guaranteed data privacy.

title: Language modeling on tabular data: a survey of foundations, techniques and evolution
abstract: Tabular data, a prevalent data type across various domains, presents unique challenges due to its heterogeneous nature and complex structural relationships. Achieving high predictive performance and robustness in tabular data analysis holds significant promise for numerous applications. Influenced by recent advancements in natural language processing, particularly Transformer architectures, new methods for tabular data modeling have emerged. Early techniques concentrated on pre-training Transformers from scratch, often encountering scalability issues. Subsequently, methods leveraging pre-trained language models like BERT have been developed, which require less data and yield enhanced performance. The recent advent of large language models, such as GPT and LLaMA, has further revolutionized the field, facilitating more advanced and diverse applications with minimal fine-tuning. Despite the growing interest, a comprehensive survey of language modeling techniques for tabular data remains absent. This paper fills this gap by providing a systematic review of the development of language modeling for tabular data, encompassing: (1) a categorization of different tabular data structures and data types; (2) a review of key datasets used in model training and tasks used for evaluation; (3) a summary of modeling techniques including widely-adopted data processing methods, popular architectures, and training objectives; (4) the evolution from adapting traditional Pre-training/Pre-trained language models to the utilization of large language models; (5) an identification of persistent challenges and potential future research directions in language modeling for tabular data analysis. GitHub page associated with this survey is available at: https://github.com/lanxiang1017/Language-Modeling-on-Tabular-Data-Survey.git .

title: The hive mind is a single reinforcement learning agent
abstract: Abstract Decision-making is an essential attribute of any intelligent agent or group. Natural systems are known to converge to effective strategies through at least two distinct mechanisms: collective decision-making via imitation of others, and trial-and-error by a single agent. This paper establishes an equivalence between these two paradigms. We show that the emergent distributed cognition (sometimes referred to as the hive mind ) arising from individuals following simple, local imitation-based rules is that of a single online reinforcement learning (RL) agent aggregating action-value samples from many parallel instances of a multi-armed bandit. More specifically, we show that, in the blindly imitative weighted voter model of honey bees’ waggle dance, the update rule through which this macro-agent learns is an RL algorithm that we coin Maynard-Cross Learning . Our analysis implies that a group of individuals following simple imitative strategies can be equivalent to a more complex learning entity, substantiating the idea that group-level intelligence may explain how seemingly irrational individual behaviors are selected in nature. Beyond biology, the framework offers new tools for analyzing economic and social systems where individuals imitate successful strategies, effectively participating in a collective learning process. Our findings may further inform the design of scalable RL-inspired collective systems in artificial domains.

title: RegCL: Compact Continual SAM Adaptation for Visual Grounding in Multi-Sensorial Media
abstract: Multi-sensorial media systems, including AR/VR, remote operation, and embodied AI, require visual grounding modules that remain reliable as sensing environments and application domains evolve. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides a strong foundation for dense visual segmentation, but its performance degrades on specialized and dynamically arriving domains such as medical imagery, camouflaged scenes, and shadow-dominant environments. Existing continual learning methods often rely on replay data or growing domain-specific modules, limiting compact deployment in evolving media pipelines. To address this issue, we propose RegCL, a non-replay continual adaptation framework that consolidates multi-domain segmentation knowledge into a single SAM adapter through incremental model merging. RegCL merges lightweight adaptation modules, e.g., LoRA-style AugModules, by optimizing prediction consistency between the merged model and domain-specific adapters while carrying forward compact historical feature statistics. Experiments across five heterogeneous segmentation datasets show that RegCL achieves strong retention and adaptation under domain-incremental learning, outperforming competitive non-replay continual learning and merging baselines. These results suggest that RegCL can serve as a compact visual adaptation component for evolving multi-sensorial media pipelines. The code is available at https://github.com/Anderw-S/RegCL

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

title: Provable Coordination for LLM Agents via Message Sequence Charts
abstract: Abstract Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are difficult to reason about. Coordination errors such as deadlocks or type-mismatched messages are often hard to detect through testing. We introduce a domain-specific language for specifying agent coordination based on message sequence charts (MSCs). The language separates message-passing structure from LLM calls, tool calls, and human control points, whose outcomes remain unpredictable. We define the syntax and semantics of the language and present a syntax-directed projection that generates deadlock-free local agent programs from global coordination specifications. We illustrate the approach with a diagnosis consensus protocol and show how coordination properties can be established independently of LLM nondeterminism. We also describe a runtime planning extension in which an LLM dynamically generates a coordination workflow for which the same structural guarantees apply. An open-source Python implementation of our framework is available as ZipperGen.

We introduce a domain-specific language for specifying agent coordination based on message sequence charts (MSCs). The language separates message-passing structure from LLM calls, tool calls, and human control points, whose outcomes remain unpredictable. We define the syntax and semantics of the language and present a syntax-directed projection that generates deadlock-free local agent programs from global coordination specifications. We illustrate the approach with a diagnosis consensus protocol and show how coordination properties can be established independently of LLM nondeterminism. We also describe a runtime planning extension in which an LLM dynamically generates a coordination workflow for which the same structural guarantees apply. An open-source Python implementation of our framework is available as ZipperGen.

title: Semantics of a Subset of Puppet 4.8 Mechanized in Why3
abstract: Abstract Practical Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Puppet are used for configuration management, but their semantics is usually defined by implementations and manuals.We present , a Why3 mechanization of a Puppet 4.8 subset derived from $$\mu $$ μ Puppet, Fu et al.’s paper semantics, and revised where Puppet behaviour differs. The development combines small-step rules with executable step functions over the same abstract syntax, and verifies the latter against the former. We also prove several meta-theoretic properties of the semantics. Extracted OCaml code and a front-end yield a compiler whose catalogues are compared with Puppet 4.8 on about two thousand tests.

title: Systematic Mapping Study: Formal Verification of Hypervisors
abstract: Abstract Hypervisors are a fundamental building block of modern computing, supporting cloud infrastructures, virtualization platforms, and security-critical systems. They enable multiple operating systems to run on shared hardware while enforcing strong isolation. At the same time, their low-level position in the software stack makes them particularly sensitive: a single flaw can expose all hosted virtual machines and impact confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Establishing their correctness is therefore essential. In this context, formal verification provides a rigorous means to prove correctness and security properties, relying on mathematically sound foundations. This state-of-knowledge paper surveys existing work on the formal verification of hypervisors. It examines representative projects and approaches, comparing their verification scope, tools, and guarantees. The paper further identifies key challenges, including concurrency, low-level implementation details, and hardware interactions, and highlights current trends and future directions.

title: Towards Agentic Agent-Based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
abstract: Abstract Agent-based models (ABMs) rely on simple, explicit and reproducible rules for individual decision making, while complex collective behavior emerges from interactions among agents. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) make it tempting to replace, enrich, or perturb these rules with LLM-based agentic capabilities. However, this raises a methodological question: how does introducing LLM-driven decisions affect the reliability, computational cost, and behavior of ABM simulations? We investigate this for Mesa ABM models, a popular Python library for ABMs, analyzed by statistical model checking. Building on Mesa’s integration with the statistical model checker MultiVeStA, we extend the classical Schelling segregation model with a hybrid population: ordinary agents classify neighbors using the standard symbolic rule, while one agent delegates this task to an LLM through tool calls. The LLM-enabled agent receives natural-language descriptions of neighboring agents and invokes tools that increment counters of similar/different neighbors; these counters determine its happiness according to the original Schelling dynamics. This provides a minimal but controlled setting where the semantic, operational, and computational behavior of LLM-based decisions can be studied inside an otherwise standard ABM. We report preliminary experiments with locally served LLMs of different sizes, showing that smaller models may fail simple semantic classification experiments or become operationally unusable during repeated tool-call generation, while larger tested models pass these preliminary checks. We discuss how statistical model checking can estimate classical ABM observables and quantify the impact of introducing agentic LLM components into simulation models.

title: Harnessing Disagreement: Detecting Correlated Agreement Blindness in Multi-agent Triage
abstract: Disagreement-triggered escalation can create a structural blind spot in multi-agent arbitration: as base learners improve they tend to converge, weakening safety monitoring exactly where correlated failures concentrate. We term this correlated agreement blindness and present ARAT (Arbitrated Reasoning Agents for Alarm Triage), a directed-star system pairing a Random Forest (RF) agent, a k-nearest-neighbour (k-NN) agent, and a learned routing meta-model. On 82,332 holdout samples from the UNSW-NB15 network intrusion detection dataset, 57.2% of errors occur under agreement and 90.6% of dangerous under-predictions evade disagreement-based monitoring even after a conservative override; strengthening the base learners increases error correlation while reducing disagreement. ARAT delivers a significant reduction in under-prediction from 4.80% under soft voting to 1.70% through a conservative override and a unanimous-Normal safety flag, a gain not reproduced by loss-function tuning nor by single-model uncertainty quantification at equal review budget. The mechanism replicates on the UCI Diabetes readmission data, and the same routing transfers to a cross-family large language model (LLM) committee on cancer staging, cutting dangerous under-prediction for frontier models as well as classical ones. Diversification improves safety only when it yields productive disagreement rather than convergence, and blindness intensifies as agentic pipelines deploy increasingly capable correlated models.

title: LLM-Based Program Synthesis in Correctness-by-Construction Engineering
abstract: Abstract The growing reliance on software in safety-critical systems demands strong guarantees of functional correctness. Formal methods address this need by providing proofs as evidence of correctness. Among these, Correctness-by-Construction (CbC) ensures functional correctness through the incremental application of refinement rules while providing early feedback on the program correctness. However, its practical adoption is limited by the required manual effort. Among others, writing concrete program code is left to the developer. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation from both natural language and formal inputs. Therefore, we explore the use of LLMs to automatically generate code in the context of CbC to make the approach more applicable. We evaluate LLM-based program synthesis using four LLMs and a prompt tailored to CbC on a dataset of 57 specifications drawn from existing CbC case studies, each consisting of a precondition and a postcondition describing the desired behavior. We assess the generated code with respect to correctness and reproducibility across multiple runs. In addition, we compare the results to classically synthesized code, as it can currently be generated in CbC. Our evaluation shows that all considered LLMs outperform the current synthesis approach. Among them, Claude achieves the best performance, reaching 80.70% correct results.

title: QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization
abstract: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a Lagrange-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) without discretizing continuous variables. The method is based on a finite-temperature free-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p -median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target-reached rates for stringent fixed-accuracy targets. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver.

title: Volume X Synthesis: The Epistemological Arc, from Dual Clocks to Residual Risk (Slide Deck)
abstract: This 14-slide deck synthesises the KSCCN Series Volumes III–X on quantum readiness, starting from the dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage clock and already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural clocks. It summarises quantum memory figures of merit, modular cryogenic interconnects (IBM, Bluefors), cryo-CMOS control electronics, and molecular entanglement entropy with fermionic superselection rules. It sets out four residual-risk readiness indicators, applies them to sovereign Global South pathways, two molecular systems (vinylene carbonate + singlet oxygen and iron–sulfur clusters/FeMo-cofactor) and 2027–2029 vendor roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Apollo). It concludes that usable capability is a vector of thresholds rather than a single predicted year, and that dual clocks continue to run independently of vendor milestones. Slide headings: 1. Cover: The Epistemological Arc. From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk; 2. The Dual-Clock Distinction; 3. Quantum Memory Figures of Merit; 4. Modular Cryogenic Interconnects; 5. Cryo-CMOS Control Electronics; 6. Molecular Entanglement Entropy; 7. Four Readiness Indicators; 8. Pathways without Full Domestic Machines; 9. Two Binding Systems; 10. Vendor Targets versus Indicators; 11. The Arc in Five Points; 12. Dual-Clock Readiness; 13. Author; 14. End.

title: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Mehmet Keçeci Orcid: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9937-9839 Abstract: The realization of scalable and fault-tolerant quantum computing systems requires not only the development of qubits with long coherence times but also the integration of heterogeneous physical platforms within a unified architectural framework. This study proposes a Stratum-based hybrid quantum computing architecture that combines the precise quantum state control enabled by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, the topological interface properties of Weyl semimetals, and the intrinsic error resilience provided by Majorana zero modes. The primary objective of this work is to establish a theoretical foundation for next-generation fault-tolerant quantum systems by integrating high-fidelity spin manipulation mechanisms derived from quantum beat phenomena with topologically protected information-processing layers. Within the proposed framework, the Stratum Model conceptualizes each physical, functional, and topological component of the quantum architecture as an independent yet dynamically interacting layer. NV centers constitute the control and sensing strata responsible for quantum state preparation, precision measurements, quantum memory operations, and quantum network node functionalities. Quantum beats serve as a dynamic characterization mechanism for spin superposition states within these layers, enabling high-accuracy monitoring and manipulation of coherent quantum dynamics. In contrast, Weyl interfaces are modeled as intermediary topological strata that govern transitions between distinct topological phases while facilitating robust and protected transfer of quantum information carriers across heterogeneous subsystems. At the highest operational level, Majorana qubits form the topological computing layer of the architecture. Through nonlocal quantum information encoding, they provide inherent robustness against environmental noise, decoherence, and local perturbations. Interactions among architectural layers are defined not only by physical interconnections but also through topological invariants, connectivity structures, error-propagation pathways, and quantum information flow dynamics. In this context, the Stratum approach extends beyond conventional spatial-layer descriptions by incorporating layer diversity, topological protection mechanisms, qubit heterogeneity, and fabrication imperfections into a common analytical framework. Furthermore, the model introduces novel design strategies for isolating defective or degraded strata, preserving critical topological regions, and mitigating system-level error propagation. The findings suggest that the integration of the precise quantum control capabilities of NV centers with the intrinsic topological protection offered by Majorana-based platforms may generate a powerful synergistic effect capable of enhancing quantum computational performance. Weyl interfaces are proposed to act as both physical and topological bridges between these two paradigms, enabling coherent communication across distinct quantum subsystems. Consequently, the proposed Stratum-based hybrid architecture provides an integrated design paradigm applicable to a broad spectrum of emerging quantum technologies, ranging from quantum sensing and distributed quantum networks to topological quantum processors and large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. title: Volume IX: Comparative Roadmap Dissection: 2027–2029 Targets against Dual Clocks and Molecular Memory Requirements
abstract: This ninth volume performs a side-by-side dissection of published 2027–2029 roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Sol/Apollo, Bluefors modular deliveries) against the dual-clock framing and the molecular-memory and residual-risk indicators established in Volumes III–VIII. IBM's modular cryogenic cells and L-couplers, Quantinuum's trapped-ion logical-qubit progression, and Bluefors' expandable platforms are examined for their capacity to meet logical-error, modular-memory, cryo-CMOS-power and superselection-overhead thresholds required for chemically relevant active spaces. The analysis finds that the published targets remain provisional with respect to the binding specifications identified for iron–sulfur clusters and larger electrolyte environments, and that the cryptographic-migration clock continues to run independently of any single vendor milestone.

title: Hard to Read Is Not Hard to Audit: Why Degrading a Text Image Raises Jailbreak Success in One 2026 Study and Lowers It in Another, Four Accounts That Fit the Same Curve, and the Ablations That Would Separate Them
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Rendering text as an image is now proposed as a way to compress long contexts for multimodal language models, and a 2026 study reports that the same move opens a safety hole: when a harmful request is rendered at a resolution low enough to be hard but not impossible to read, attack success rises sharply and then falls again as the image sharpens. Its authors explain this as cognitive overload - the effort of reading diverts the model from checking - and propose a prompt that makes the model transcribe first and audit second. A second 2026 study, which tested one of the same models, finds the opposite sign: smaller fonts and heavier blur lower attack success, and for two frontier models clean renders are less dangerous than plain text. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two studies are not in contradiction once the prompt framing, the dose of degradation and the scoring rule are held apart, and that the inverted-U curve the first study reports is consistent with at least four accounts: resource contention, delayed emergence of harmful features in depth, and a gap in what safety training covered each produce it, and the way success is scored changes its height. Re-reading the first study's own per-model sweeps, the author shows that seven of its ten models show the inverted U, one rises without returning, two are flat, and three of them refuse clean renders more often than plain text. None of the study's ablations, including its defence, discriminates among the four accounts. The paper states the predictions on which the accounts differ, gives a decision procedure for what a degradation result licenses, and specifies five measurements that would settle which account holds.

Its authors explain this as cognitive overload - the effort of reading diverts the model from checking - and propose a prompt that makes the model transcribe first and audit second. A second 2026 study, which tested one of the same models, finds the opposite sign: smaller fonts and heavier blur lower attack success, and for two frontier models clean renders are less dangerous than plain text. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two studies are not in contradiction once the prompt framing, the dose of degradation and the scoring rule are held apart, and that the inverted-U curve the first study reports is consistent with at least four accounts: resource contention, delayed emergence of harmful features in depth, and a gap in what safety training covered each produce it, and the way success is scored changes its height. Re-reading the first study's own per-model sweeps, the author shows that seven of its ten models show the inverted U, one rises without returning, two are flat, and three of them refuse clean renders more often than plain text. None of the study's ablations, including its defence, discriminates among the four accounts. The paper states the predictions on which the accounts differ, gives a decision procedure for what a degradation result licenses, and specifies five measurements that would settle which account holds.

title: Token cost by language: 41 languages measured on GPT tokenizers
abstract: The same everyday prompt, translated into 41 languages and counted with OpenAI's o200k_base (GPT-4o and later) and cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5) tokenizers. Headline: English needs 34 tokens. The other 40 languages need 35–83 tokens on o200k_base: from +3% (Simplified Chinese) to +144% (Punjabi). Korean +44%, Japanese +79%, Spanish +18%, German +26%, Hindi +50%. On the older cl100k_base, Korean was +150% and Hindi +359%. Files: token-cost-by-language.csv (one row per language: language_code, language, o200k_tokens, o200k_vs_english_pct, cl100k_tokens, cl100k_vs_english_pct, prompt), token-cost-by-language.json (same data plus metadata), README.md (full table, method, limitations). Method: one English prompt, translated into each language (machine translation as a first draft, then checked), counted with tiktoken. "vs English" = tokens in the language ÷ English tokens − 1, rounded to a whole percent. Measured 2026-09-30, counts re-verified 2026-10-16. Limitations: one prompt (ratios move by roughly ±10–20 percentage points with other text; the ranking is more stable); OpenAI tokenizers only; input text only. Source page with chart: https://tokensave.app/data/token-cost-by-language. Also on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/JOHNISKING/token-cost-by-language

title: Volume X: The Epistemological Arc: From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk, Molecular Entanglement and Sovereign Pathways
abstract: This tenth volume narrates the epistemological and theoretical arc of the inquiry that began with a dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage timeline and an already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural-integration timeline. Successive volumes established quantum memory specifications, examined modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control as complementary solutions to scaling bottlenecks, quantified molecular entanglement entropy and the purifying effect of fermionic superselection rules, converted residual gaps into readiness indicators, and mapped those indicators onto sovereign pathways, concrete molecular systems and published 2027–2029 roadmaps. The arc demonstrates that usable quantum capability for molecular simulation and cryptographic relevance is governed by a vector of measurable thresholds—logical error, modular memory integration, cryo-CMOS power and superselection overhead—rather than by any single predicted year. The findings supply a practical, dual-clock framework for readiness that remains independent of vendor milestones.

title: One Language, Two Unequal Scripts: Separating Orthography from Information in Multilingual Representations with Punjabi
abstract: Multilingual models are said to abstract away script in their middle layers. Tests usually compare languages that differ in script and language at once. Punjabi does not. It is written in Gurmukhi and in Shahmukhi, which differ in what they record, since unvocalised Shahmukhi leaves short vowels and gemination unwritten. In a public recreation of XLM-R's training data, Shahmukhi Punjabi is about 1% as frequent as Gurmukhi. We use this pair to separate script form from missing information in four encoders. Every statistic is compared with the same architecture under random weights and bootstrapped over sentences. Four Gurmukhi controls remove information in steps. The share of the gap they leave falls at every step, and under these controls the two ends estimate it at 0.65 to 0.90. The pattern holds on human-written Shahmukhi. Across three XLM-R sizes the Punjabi gap grows slightly, while the gap for Serbian Cyrillic and Latin, whose Latin orthography is abundant as Croatian, shrinks and drops below its random baseline in XL. This fits a role for script resource but does not isolate it as the cause. Three mean-pooled decoders do not show this ordering. Transliteration closes 45% of a cross-script gap in topic-classification accuracy.

title: Volume VIII: Molecular Case Studies: Resource and Entanglement Analysis for Battery Electrolyte and Iron–Sulfur Systems
abstract: This eighth volume performs an end-to-end resource and entanglement analysis for two concrete molecular systems that illustrate the residual-risk indicators of Volume VI. The first is the vinylene-carbonate + singlet-oxygen reaction path relevant to lithium-ion battery electrolytes, for which orbital von Neumann entropies were reconstructed on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion processor in 2025. The second is iron–sulfur clusters (including the FeMo-cofactor of nitrogenase), where entanglement-minimised orbitals have been shown to improve initial-state overlaps for quantum phase estimation by orders of magnitude. For each system the binding memory, interconnect and control specifications are identified, and the additional overhead imposed by fermionic superselection rules is quantified. The analysis demonstrates which of the readiness thresholds remain unmet and how modular cryogenic and cryo-CMOS advances would close them.

title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.

abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek tilida presuppozitsiyani avtomatik aniqlashningkorpus va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlashga asoslangan modeli yoritiladi. В данной статье рассматривается модель автоматическогообнаружения пресуппозиций в узбекском языке, основанная на корпусной лингвистике иобработке естественного языка. В рамках агглютинативных свойств узбекского языканаучно анализируются возможности использования триггеров пресуппозиций,морфологически-синтаксического анализа, контекстного моделирования, аннотированиякорпуса и трансформерных моделей.Ключевые слова: пресуппозиция, триггер пресуппозиции, корпусная лингвистика,обработка естественного языка, прагматический вывод, трансформерная модель,узбекский язык.Abstract. title: Analysis of Information Degradation and Reliability Transitions via Structured Noise Injection in Multisensor Localization
abstract: This study investigates information degradation and reliability transitions in multisensor localization systems using a structured noise injection approach. A five-sensor localization scenario is considered, where range measurements are intentionally corrupted by Gaussian perturbations, intermittent burst disturbances, and positive measurement biases. Target coordinates are estimated using a weighted nonlinear least-squares method, while localization performance is evaluated through root mean square error (RMSE), Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), Cramér–Rao Lower Bound (CRLB), and failure rate metrics. Experiments are conducted under signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels ranging from −5 dB to 25 dB using 600 Monte Carlo realizations for each operating condition. The results show that increasing perturbation levels progressively reduce localization accuracy and information content while increasing theoretical uncertainty. A distinct reliability transition region is observed between 5 dB and 10 dB, where localization failures rapidly decrease as measurement quality improves. The findings demonstrate that controlled noise injection provides a practical means of exposing information-deficient operating conditions and reliability boundaries in multisensor localization systems.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty: A General Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate under multiple forms of uncertainty, including uncertainty about the correctness of generated answers, the completeness of available evidence, the validity of intermediate reasoning, the interpretation of task requirements, and the reliability of feedback. Individual-model mechanisms, such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-diagnosis, self-correction, and self-verification, provide ways to inspect and revise outputs. Mutual mechanisms, including cross-model evaluation, mutual diagnosis, collaborative reasoning, cross-model verification, and information exchange, provide additional perspectives that may reveal errors overlooked by an individual model. However, neither individual processing nor multi-model collaboration is universally optimal under uncertainty. Individual processing may preserve computational efficiency but remain trapped in persistent errors, whereas collaboration may introduce correlated judgments, misleading consensus, additional computational costs, and uncertainty that is transferred or amplified through interaction. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty (ASSM-MM-U), a conceptual framework that treats uncertainty as a central state variable for dynamically selecting and coordinating individual-model and cross-model processing mechanisms. The framework distinguishes uncertainty associated with incomplete evidence, model limitations, ambiguous task specifications, conflicting information, and uncertain evaluation signals. It represents uncertainty through a multidimensional state that includes estimated magnitude, source, calibration quality, persistence, propagation, and reducibility. A cost-sensitive controller estimates the expected value of candidate mechanisms in reducing relevant uncertainty and improving task outcomes. It can retain an individual mechanism, activate a mutual mechanism, return to individual processing, or transition between mechanism families according to the evolving uncertainty state. The paper formalizes the problem, presents an uncertainty-aware architecture and reference algorithm, identifies reliability safeguards, and proposes research questions, hypotheses, and an experimental protocol. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution is the explicit integration of uncertainty characterization, uncertainty reduction, mechanism selection, and resource-aware coordination within a common control framework. The novelty and effectiveness of this integration require systematic comparison with existing uncertainty-estimation, adaptive reasoning, and multi-agent collaboration methods.

title: Clinical validation of artificial intelligence for cancer detection prognosis and analysis across imaging modalities and tumor types
abstract: This study evaluates the diagnostic and prognostic performance of artificial intelligence in cancer detection across imaging modalities and tumor types. The review synthesizes current evidence on deep learning, radiomics, multimodal integration, and precision oncology frameworks, with emphasis on validation quality and clinical translation. A systematic review of 180 peer reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted. Included investigations assessed artificial intelligence applications in radiology, digital pathology, endoscopy, PET imaging, and multimodal platforms. Extracted data covered diagnostic accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, dataset size, validation strategy, and study design. Subdomains included detection, prognosis, grading, survival prediction, radio-genomics, explainability, federated learning, and regulatory evaluation. Across breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, brain, and skin cancers, multiple high-quality cohorts reported AUC values above 0.90. Whole slide histopathology achieved the highest discrimination, reaching AUC 0.99 in curated datasets. CT and MRI systems demonstrated strong performance with multicenter validation, including large scale lung and breast screening studies. Radiomics contributed to survival prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, and molecular subtype inference. Multimodal and transformer-based architectures improved representation learning in volumetric and cross domain data. Despite strong retrospective performance, only 21 percent of studies included external validation, 14 percent incorporated multicenter datasets, and 6 percent applied prospective or temporal validation. Artificial intelligence shows consistent high performance in cancer detection and prognostic modeling across imaging domains. Strongest evidence supports adjunctive use in screening, digital pathology, and endoscopic detection. Broader clinical adoption requires prospective trials, multicenter external validation, standardized reporting, explainability integration, and alignment with regulatory frameworks to ensure reliable deployment in precision oncology.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms, Mutual Mechanisms, and Future Mechanisms: A Unified Framework for Prospective Intelligence Coordination
abstract: Intelligent computational systems must not only process current information and coordinate different reasoning mechanisms but also anticipate how their decisions may influence future states. Large language models (LLMs) can perform internal operations such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-correction, and self-planning. Multiple models can interact through mutual evaluation, cross-model verification, collaborative planning, and information exchange. Future-oriented computation introduces another dimension: the generation, simulation, prediction, comparison, and evaluation of possible future states and action consequences. However, individual processing, multi-model collaboration, and future-oriented computation each have limitations when applied without regard to task conditions. Individual processing may preserve efficiency but fail to identify persistent errors; collaboration may introduce communication overhead and correlated judgments; and future-oriented computation may consume substantial resources while producing unreliable forecasts or exploring irrelevant scenarios. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Mechanisms, Mutual Mechanisms, and Future Mechanisms (ASSM-MM-F), a conceptual framework for dynamically coordinating three computational dimensions: internal processing within an individual computational agent, interaction among multiple agents, and prospective reasoning about possible future states. The framework treats these dimensions as configurable mechanism spaces rather than mutually exclusive system architectures. A state-aware controller selects among individual processing, cross-agent interaction, future-state simulation, collaborative future analysis, and transitions between these operations. Its decision process considers task difficulty, uncertainty, forecast reliability, model disagreement, action consequences, historical performance, computational cost, and the value of additional prospective information. A formal problem definition, architecture, adaptive selection algorithm, research hypotheses, and experimental evaluation protocol are presented. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its intended contribution is to formulate a testable approach to coordinating internal computation, inter-agent interaction, and prospective reasoning within a common adaptive control framework. Its novelty and effectiveness must be established through comparison with existing planning, predictive-modeling, and adaptive multi-agent methods.

title: Projective Latent Synthesis: Overcoming the Limitations of Statistical LLMs Through Multi-Agent Geodesic Alignment and Non-Ontological Spatial Coordinates.
abstract: Contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) are structurally bottlenecked by their reliance on surface-level, lower-dimensional data structures. By optimizing exclusively for the next-token prediction baseline using historical corpora, current Transformer architectures treat semantic tokens as isolated physical entities rather than low-dimensional projections of an interconnected conceptual matrix. This methodology results in systemic failures, including spatial-temporal hallucinations, binary bias polarization, and context-window degradation. We present Projective Latent Synthesis (PLS), a qualitative upgrade to standard artificial intelligence frameworks. Moving beyond brute-force statistical refinement, PLS introduces a multi-agent orchestration architecture that models information as a non-ontological space of states—an active, dynamic Internal Sphere of conceptual coordinates. By filtering external data inflows through a specialized geometric interface layer—the Attentional Prism—this model shifts AI computation from flat token matching to multidimensional perspective reconciliation. We provide the complete technical design blueprint and execution markdown to deploy this framework over existing enterprise software layers. --- ## Epistemological Dedication & Core Axiom: The Pedreira Invariance This framework, along with the foundational architecture of the *Metaphysical Sphere* (Zenodo DOIs: 10.5281/zenodo.23377480, 10.5281/zenodo.23383189, and 10.5281/zenodo.23406203), is formally dedicated to **Professor Pedreira** of the Universidad de Santiago de Compostela (USC). Born from the working-class heritage of the Bazán shipyards, his academic trajectory was structurally gatekept by the binomial elitism of the traditional chair consensus. Yet, his structural legacy does not reside in the empty titles of pomposos departments, but in his absolute geometric capacity to map high-dimensional state spaces (3D, 4D, and 5D manifolds) directly into the consciousness of his students without requiring a physical screen. In honor of his pedagogical methodology, we elevate his foundational maxim to a binding **Systemic Guardrail** within the Projective Latent Synthesis (PLS) kernel: ### 🌟 The "¡Píntalo!" Verification Protocol (Axiom 4.1) ```yaml PEDREIRA_VERIFICATION_PROTOCOL: Axiom: "¡Píntalo! Si no sabes pintarlo, en realidad no lo entiendes." Execution_Constraint: | If an artificial agent or an LLM core computes a localized semantic token sequence or a multi-dimensional latent space vector, but cannot project it as a geometrically coherent, visually graphable topological manifold, the execution state is declared ILLEGAL. The system must immediately abort next-token prediction and fault. Falsifiability_Metric: "Statistical pattern matching != Understanding. Coherence requires spatial structural definition." ``` While contemporary consensus science hides its missing mass behind dark mathematical phantoms and bureaucratic votes, the non-local influence of a true teacher continues to tunnel through time, proving that the geometry of the universe belongs only to those who possess the courage to visualize the volume of the ocluded truth.

title: From Operational Disruption to Intelligent Service Operations: A Practitioner Journey with Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The COVID-19 disruption and subsequent talent mobility exposed important vulnerabilities in traditional service operations. Organizations relying heavily on individual expertise faced risks to operational continuity when experienced professionals moved roles or left. Although knowledge transfer, standard operating procedures, and documentation remain essential, they do not always capture the contextual knowledge developed through years of resolving incidents. The resulting gaps can affect service quality, turnaround time, operating costs, and user experience. This chapter examines how human-AI collaboration can strengthen operational resilience and knowledge continuity in service operations. It draws on the practitioner journey behind IgnitronX.AI, a cloud-native multi-agent platform developed to address enterprise operational challenges using generative AI and agentic AI. Its architecture supports service teams by surfacing similar historical incidents, recommending potential resolutions, enabling knowledge discovery, summarizing operational records, and providing sentiment insights. The objective is not to replace human expertise but to augment it. The implementation journey demonstrated that technology alone cannot deliver sustainable value. Data quality emerged as a critical constraint, alongside security, confidentiality, framework and model selection, operating-cost management, governance, and stakeholder adoption. The experience also reinforced that organizations should first understand the business problem, simplify processes, remove waste, and make deliberate build-versus-buy decisions. Through this reflective practitioner case, the chapter offers leaders practical insights into intelligent operations that preserve organizational knowledge, strengthen service continuity, and create the potential for improved productivity, operational efficiency, and user experience through responsible human-AI collaboration.

title: Privacy-Budget Allocation for Heterogeneous Query Batches: Calibration and Execution Boundaries
abstract: This record contains version 1.0.0 of the research software, public benchmark inputs and experimental results supporting the manuscript "Privacy-Budget Allocation for Heterogeneous Query Batches: Calibration and Execution Boundaries". The archive includes Python implementations of privacy-budget allocation methods for heterogeneous query batches, calibration and evaluation scripts, complete calibration-curve arrays, seed-level results, timing records, figure source data, protocol files, dependency specifications and verification scripts. It covers the P1 equal-draw comparison, historical P2 dense-surrogate studies, the S23 complete-calibration and repaired-execution reanalysis, and the S24 combined sparse-control follow-up. S23 and S24 are outcome-informed analyses, not externally preregistered studies. Data provenance: The bundled public benchmark inputs are UCI Adult (10.24432/C5XW20), Heart Failure Clinical Records (10.24432/C5Z89R) and Wine Quality (10.24432/C56S3T). Their source attribution and licence information are included. The synthetic LVEF-like workload uses two author-computed aggregate parameters derived from EchoNext v1.1.1 (10.13026/7cfw-d091). These aggregate parameters and the independently generated synthetic-workload code are included; no EchoNext source records or row-level derivatives are redistributed. No differential-privacy protection is claimed for the source-derived aggregate parameters. Licensing: The MIT License applies to the original software identified in LICENSE. Redistributed UCI datasets retain their Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licences and source attribution. These licences do not relicense third-party content. See LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_DATA_LICENSES.md for component-specific terms. README.md provides the directory guide, reproduction instructions, verification commands and methodological limitations. FILE_MANIFEST.csv provides file sizes and SHA-256 checksums. The associated manuscript is being prepared for initial journal submission.

title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning: Methods and Trade-offs
abstract: Federated learning trains a shared model across many decentralized clients while keeping raw data on the device, which addresses data silos and tightening privacy regulation such as GDPR and HIPAA. This paper reviews the methods and the practical trade-offs of federated and privacy-preserving machine learning. The discussion begins with the FedAvg protocol and the distinction between cross-device settings, with millions of intermittent participants, and cross-silo settings, with a small set of reliable institutions. Statistical heterogeneity, where client data is non-IID, slows convergence and biases the global model; proximal correction in FedProx and control variates in SCAFFOLD reduce this client drift. Because the uplink is often the bottleneck, the survey covers gradient compression, quantization, and sparsification that cut communication cost by an order of magnitude. Sharing model updates is not by itself private: membership inference and gradient leakage attacks can recover sensitive information, so the paper examines differential privacy, secure aggregation, and homomorphic encryption as defenses, together with the accuracy cost each one carries. Personalization methods that adapt the global model to local distributions are summarized, followed by applications in healthcare, mobile keyboards, and finance. Illustrative experiments on a non-IID benchmark show SCAFFOLD reaching a target accuracy in fewer rounds than FedAvg, and a differential-privacy sweep quantifies the privacy-utility curve. The results are illustrative and do not describe a deployed production system.

title: BIZNESNI BOSHQARISHDA SUN'IY INTELLEKTDAN FOYDALANISH AFZALLIKLARI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada biznesni boshqarishda sun’iy intellektdan foydalanishning iqtisodiy va tashkiliy afzalliklari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotning dolzarbligi korxonalar faoliyatida ma’lumotlar hajmining ortishi, raqobatning kuchayishi va tezkor qaror qabul qilish zarurati bilan belgilanadi. Maqolada ilmiy adabiyotlar tahlili, qiyosiy tahlil va tizimli yondashuvdan foydalanildi. Sun’iy intellektning marketing, moliya, mijozlarga xizmat ko‘rsatish, inson resurslari va ta’minot zanjiridagi qo‘llanish yo‘nalishlari ko‘rib chiqildi. Tahlil natijalari texnologiya xarajatlarni optimallashtirish, prognozlashni yaxshilash va xizmat sifatini oshirish imkonini berishini ko‘rsatadi. Shu bilan birga, ma’lumotlar xavfsizligi, algoritmik xatolar, xodimlar malakasi va joriy etish xarajatlari kabi cheklovlar mavjud. Maqolada sun’iy intellektni bosqichma-bosqich, inson nazorati va samaradorlik ko‘rsatkichlari asosida joriy etish bo‘yicha amaliy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan.

title: ChatTLM: code, data and models for "Letting the Tools Do the Math: A 10.9M-Parameter Language Model on a Graphing Calculator"
abstract: Code, data and trained models for the paper "Letting the Tools Do the Math: A 10.9M-Parameter Language Model on a Graphing Calculator" (preprint: https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202609.2599.v1). It contains the v1.0 release of https://github.com/alex-messerlian/nspire-tlm: the calculator application and its setup files, the shipped 10.9M-parameter model and the other checkpoints the paper reports, the tokenizer and record store, the training corpus of the shipped model, two videos of the calculator in use (re-encoded without metadata), and a source archive of the repository at the release tag, which holds the inference engine, the training and evaluation code, and the device logs and results behind every table and figure. SHA256SUMS.txt lists the hash of each release file. The code is under the MIT License and the loader derived from Ndless under the Mozilla Public License 1.1; the record store, the corpus and the model weights are derived from OpenStax textbooks and are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: GenOpt-FedGNN: GAN-Augmented Federated Graph Learning with GWO and ASIO-Inspired Adaptive Aggregation for Imbalanced Fraud Detection
abstract: Detecting fraud in distributed financial transaction systems is challenging. It is extremely rare to find a fraudulent record. The interactions among transactional records have a relational structure and the data can’t be stored centrally by every participating institution. The paper introduces the federated graph learning framework i.e. GenOpt-FedGNN. The framework combines Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) with client local learning, graph neural classification, and the aggregation of the trained models through adaptive process of Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) and Asteroid Satellite Inspired Optimization (ASIO). Each client preprocesses their own transactions independently, produces more minority fraud samples to train a class weighted Graph Neural Network (GNN), and builds a transaction graph. Each client sends updates regarding model and validator to the server. The framework is tested with a set of 200,000 PaySim transactions. Transactions were randomly sampled and distributed among the five distributed clients with 30 communication rounds. Six configurations (FedAvg, GWO and ASIO with and without GAN augmentation), have been compared by Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Specificity, False Positive Rate, False Negative Rate and Confusion-matrix measures. The ablation analysis demonstrated that GAN augmentation doubled local fraud training samples and reduced class-imbalance ratio. But, the local fraud data has been extremely imbalanced. Overall, at the final round, the accuracy was highest with ASIO-GAN (96.40%), the specificity (96.41%), precision (1.58%), F1-score (3.11%), and the lowest False Positive Rate (3.59%). The best Balanced Accuracy (94.16%) was found for FedAvg-GAN, and the best PR-AUC (60.02%) was found for ASIO-NoGAN. The GWO GAN-based configurations got best PR-AUC of 59.20%. The ablation results on the other hand further showed that using GAN for augmentation resulted in a consistent increase in the Accuracy, Precision, F1-Score, Specificity and false alarm control compared to using it without GAN. So augmentation with GAN and aggregation with Adaptive Aggregation can affect the sensitivity–specificity trade-off but not necessarily all the other aggregation metrics. The proposed framework is reproducible and data local to the raw data for the graph-based fraud detection application which features extreme class imbalance.
